definitions.explanation: A class of synthetic gases formerly used as refrigerants and in aerosol sprays, now phased out because they damage the ozone layer. The Japanese term covers CFCs and related halogenated coolants in general usage.

examples.japanese: フロンガスは{使用|しよう}が{制限|せいげん}されている。
examples.english: The use of CFCs is restricted.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}にはフロンガスが{使|つか}われていた。
examples.english: CFCs were used in older refrigerators.

examples.japanese: フロンガスがオゾン{層|そう}を{破壊|はかい}することが{明|あき}らかになって{以来|いらい}、{国際的|こくさいてき}な{規制|きせい}が{進|すす}んだ。
examples.english: Since it became clear that CFCs destroy the ozone layer, international regulations have advanced.

notes:
フロン is the Japanese short form for fluorocarbons/freon; フロンガス is the gas form. The Montreal Protocol (1987) led to a gradual phase-out, with replacement refrigerants ({代替|だいたい}フロン) now in common use.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- フロンガスを{放出|ほうしゅつ}する: to release CFCs
- フロンガスの{回収|かいしゅう}: recovery of CFCs (legal requirement when disposing of appliances)
- フロンガス{規制|きせい}: CFC regulations
- {代替|だいたい}フロン: replacement CFCs (HFCs, HCFCs)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- オゾン{層|そう}: ozone layer — the atmospheric layer CFCs damage
- {温室効果|おんしつこうか}ガス: greenhouse gas — broader category; CFCs also contribute to warming
